And in like mannr of or espetiall grace crteine knowledge & meere moc̃õn, we haue graunted and9 doe for vs or heires and successors graunte vnto the said Gournor and Company of mrchaunte of London trading into the East Indies & their successors.

That yt shall and may be lawfull to & for the said Gournor & Companie and their successors after the said first voyadge sett forth yearelie for and during the residue of the
said terme of ffifteene yeares to shipp and transporte out of this or Realme of England or dominions of the same in any their other voyadge to or towarde any the parte aforesaid in forme afore mencioned all such forreine Coyne of sylver, spannish or other forreine sylver or bullion of sylver, as they shall duringe the said terme bringe or cause to be brought into this Realme of England in1 the pte beyond the Seas, eyther in the same kinde sorte stampe or ffashion wch yt shall haue when they bringe it in, or any other forme, stampe or fashion to be coyned wthin or Mint wthin or Tower of London at their pleasuer, soe as the whole quantities of coyne or moneys by them to be transported in any their said voyage during the residue of the said terme doe not exceede the value or some of Thirtie Thowsand pounde in any one voyage, and soe as the some of sixe thowsand pounde at the least pcell of the said some or value of xxx mli soe to be transported as aforesaid, be first coyned wthin or said Tower of London before the same shall be transported in any of the said voyage any lawe statute restrainte or phibĩcõn in that behalfe in any wyse notwthstandinge.

That the trade shalbe traded according to ye Ordenances of the Company & not otherwyse And further we of or ample and aboundant grace, more2 moc̃on and certeyne knowledge haue graunted by3 theis presente for vs or heires and successors, doe graunt vnto the said Gournor & Company of mrchaunte of London trading into the East Indies & their successors that they and their successors and their ffactors servante or assignes in the trade of mrchandize for them & on their behalfe & not otherwyse shall for the said terme of ffyfteene yeares, haue, vse, and enioy the wholle entyre & onelie trade & traffique and the wholle entire & onelie libertie vse & priviledge of tradinge & traffiqueing & vsinge feat & trade of mrchandize to & from the said East Indies & to & from all the Ilande Porte Havens Citties Townes and places aforesaid in such manner & forme as ys aboue mencioned And that4 the said Gournor & Company of mrchaunte of London tradinge into
the East Indies, & eury pticuler & seurall pson that now is, or that heerafter shalbe of that Company or incorporac̃on shall haue full and free authoritie libertie facultie lycence & power in forme aforesaid to trade & Traffique to & from the said East Indies, & all & eury the ptę thereof in forme aforesaid according to the orders ordenances & agreemte heereafter to be made & agr&ed vppon by the said Gournor & Companie of mrchauntę of London trading into the East Indies & their successors or the more ptę of them present at any Courte or publique assemblie of or for the said Companie the Gournor of the said Companie or his Deputie for the tyme beinge alwaies present att such Courte or assembly & not otherwyse.

That 6 good shipps & 6 pinnaces shalbe yearelie permitted to goe into the East Indies & 500 mariners any restraint notwthstandinge except the Nauie Royall goe forth. And for that the shipps sayleing into the said Indies must take their due & propp tymes to pceede in theis voyage wch otherwyse as we well pceaue cannot be pformed in the rest of the yeare followinge. THERFORE we of or especiall grace certeine knowledge & meere moc̃on for vs or heires & successors do graunt to & wth the said Gournor & Company of mrchauntę of London tradinge into the East Indies and their successors, that in any tyme of restrainte sixe good shipps & sixe good Pynnaces well furnished wth ordenance & other munic̃on for their defence, & fiue hundred Mariners Englishmen to guide & sayle in the same sixe shipps & sixe Pynnaces att all tymes during the said terme of fyfteene yeares shall quietlie be p̄mitted & suffered to departe & goe in the said voyages accordinge to the purport of theis prsentę wthout any stay or contradicc̃on by vs or heires or successors or by ye Lo: High admirall or any other officer or subiect of vs or heires or successors for the tyme being in any wyse any restrainte lawe statute vsage or matter whatsoeur to the contrarie notwthstandinge.

A prohibicon to all other subjectes not free of this comp: for trading into those partes upon seuerall peines wthout the licence & assent of the Companie. forfecture of goodes & shipps PROUIDED neurtheles that yf we shall att any tyme wthin the said terme of fifteene yeares, haue iust cause to arme our Navy in warlike manner in defence of or Realme or for Offence of or enymies or that yt shall be found needfull to ioyne to the Navy of vs or heires or successors the shipps of or subiectę to be alsoe armed for the warres to such a number as can not be supplied yf the said sixe shipps and sixe Pynnasses should be p̄mitted to
departe as aboue is mentioned then vpon knowledge geven to1 vs or heires or successors or by any2 Admirall to the said Gournor & Company aboute the xxth day of the monneth of Iulie, or three monnethes before the said Gournor and Companie shall begynn to make readie the same sixe shipps and sixe Pynnasses, that we may not spare the said sixe shipps & six Pynnasses & the Mariners requisite for them, to be out of or Realme during the tyme that or Navy shall be vpon the Seas. That then the said Gournor and Company shall forbeare to send sixe such shipps & sixe Pinnacę for their trade of mrchandize, vntill that we shall revoke or wthdrawe or said Navy for this3 service. And we of or further royall favor and of or especiall grace certeine knowledge and meere moc̃on haue graunted, and by theis presentę for vs or heires & successors doe graunte vnto the said Gournor & Company of mrchauntę of London tradinge into the East Indies and to their successors That the said East Indies nor the Ilandę Havens Portę Citties Townes or places thereof, nor of any pte thereof shall4 be visited frequented or haunted by any of the subiectę of vs or heires or successors during the said terme of xvteene yeares contrarie to the true meaneing of theis presentę. And by vertue of or prrogatiue royall, wch we will not in that behalfe be argued or brought in question: We straight chardge comaund and phibitt for vs or heires & successors all the subiectę of vs or heires or successors of what degree or qualitie soeur they be, that none of them directlie or indirectlie visitt haunte frequent or Trade, traffique or adventure by way of mrchandize into or from any of the said East Indies, or into & from any of the Ilandę, Portę Havens, Citties Townes or places aforesaid other then the said Gournor & Company of mrchauntę of London trading into the East Indies, and such pticuler psons as now be or heereafter shall be of that Companie their Agentę ffactors & assignes duringe the said terme of fyfteene yeares5 vnles
yt be by & wth such licence and agreement of the said Gournor & Companie of mrchaunte of London tradinge to the East Indies in wryting first had & obtayned vnder their Comon seale to be graunted, vpon payne that euery such pson or psonns that shall trade or traffique into or from any of the said East Indies other then the Gournor & Company of mrchaunte of London & their successors shall incurr or indignac̃on and the forfecture & losse of the goodes mrchaundizes & other thinge whatsoeur wch soe shall be brought into this or Realme of England or any the dominion[s] of the same contrarie to or said phibition, or the purporte or1 true meaneing of theis presente as alsoe the shipp and shipps wth the furniture thereof wherein such goode mrchaundizes or thinge shalbe brought:

Diuision of the forfectures. Imprisonmt. entring into bond of 1000li The halfe2 of all the said forfectures to be to vs or heires and successors, and the other halfe of all & eury the said forfecture[s] we doe by theis presente of or espetiall grace certeine knowledge & meere moc̃on clearlie and whollie for vs or heires and successors giue and graunte vnto the said Gournor and Companie of mrchaunte of London trading into the East Indies. And further all & eury the said Offendors for their said Contempt to suffer imprisonment duringe or pleasure and such other ponishmt as to vs or heires or successors for soe high a Contempt shall seeme meete & convenient & not to be in any wyse deliured vntill they & eury of them shalbe come bound vnto the said Gournor for the tyme being in the some of 1000li att the least at noe tyme then after during this present graunte to sayle or traffique into any of the said East Indies contrarie to or expresse Comaundement in that behalfe herein sett downe & published.

How the Comp: may graunt lycence to others & what tymes. That her matie will not graunt lycence to any others to enter into the partes aforesaid during the terme of xvteene yeares That the Company may admitt others att their pleasures into this fredome That yf any named in the pattent doe not bring in his promysed aduenture sett downe yt shall be lawfull for ye Companie to disfranchyse him. The Companie doe promyse to bring in after eury voyadge retourned wthin 6 monnethes as great a quantetie of silver gould or forraine Coyne as they shall carry out th first viadg excepted All sylver or gould1 carried forth by the Comp: shalbe shipped att the portes of London Dartmouth or Plymouth. And further for the better encouragemt of mrchaunt3 straungers & others to bringe in Comodities into this our Realme, we for vs or heires and successors doe graunt vnto the said Gournor & Companie of mrchaunte of London tradinge into the East Indies that they & their successors shall from tyme to tyme for any Considerac̃on or benefitt to be taken to their owne vse graunt or giue
licence to any pson or psons to sayle trade or traffique into or from any of the said East Indies soe as such licence be graunted or geuen before such goode wares & mrchaundizes be laid on land, & soe as such lycence be made by the said Gournor & Company of mrchaunte of London tradinge into the East Indies for the tyme beinge vnder their Comon seale. And further of or especiall grace certeyne knowledge, & meere moc̃on, we haue Condescended and graunted, and by theis presente for1 or heires and successors wee doe condescend & graunt vnto the said Gournor & Companie of mrchaunte of London tradinge into the2 East Indies and their successors that we or heires & successors during the said terme of xvteene yeares will not graunte libertie licence or power to any pson or psons whatsoeur contrary to the Tenor of theis or lres Pattente to sayle passe trade or traffique to the said East Indies or into or from the Ilande porte Havens Citties Townes or place aforesaid or any of them contrarie to the true meaneinge of theis presente wthout the Consent of the said Gournor & Company of mrchaunte of London trading into the East Indies or the most pte of them. And or will and pleasure is and hereby we doe alsoe ordeyne that that yt shall & may be lawfull to & for the said Gournor & Company of mrchaunte of London tradinge into the East Indies or the more pte of them whereof the Gournor for the tyme being or his deputie to be one to admitt into, & to be of the said Company all such apprentises to any of the said ffellowshipp or company and all such servaunte & ffactors3 of or for the said Company, & all such others as to them or the more pte of them present at any Courte held for the said Company the Gournor or his deputie being one shalbe thought ffitt and agreeable wth the orders and Ordenances to be made for the Gournmt of the said Company PROUIDED alwaies that yf any of the psons before named and appointed by theis presente to be free of the said Companie of
mrchauntę of London tradinge into the East Indies shall not before the goinge forth of the ffleete appointed for this first voyadge from the porte of London bringe in & deliur to the Thrēr or Thrērs appointed, or wch wthin the space of Twentie daies next after the date hereof shalbe appointed by the said gournor & Company or the more pte of them, to receiue the Contribucõns and adventures sett downe by the seurall Aduenturors in this first1 & present voyadge now in hand to be sett forth such somes of money as haue beene by any of the said p̱sons by theis presentę nominated to be of the said Company expressed sett downe & written in a booke appointed for that purpose, & left in the handę of the said Thomas Smyth Gournor of the said Company or of the said Paule Bannynge Ald of London and subscribed wth the names or2 of the same aduenturors vnder their handę & agreed vpon to be aduentured in the said first voyadge that then yt shall be lawfull for the said Gournor and Companie or the more pte of them, whereof the said Gournor or his deputie to be one at any their generall Courte, or generall assembly to remoue disfranchise & displace him or them att their wills and pleasures. And the said Gournor & Company of mrchauntę of London tradinge into the East Indies for them and their successors doe by theis presentę couenant p̱myse & graunte to & wth 3 or heires & successors that they the said Gournor & Company and their successors in all & eury such voyage as they att any tyme or tymes heareafter duringe the said tearme shall make out of this Realme by vertue of this or graunt and łres Pattentę the first voyadge onelie excepted shall & will vpon eury retourne wch shall be made backe agayne into this or Realme or any of or dominions or wthin sixe monnethes next after eury such retourne bringe into this or Realme of England from the said East Indies or from some other parte beyond the seas out of or Dominions, as greate or greater value in bullion of gould or syluer, or other forreyne Coyne of gould or silver respectiuelie for eury voyadge, the first voyadge
onelie excepted as shall be by force of theis presente transported and carried out of this Realme by them or any of them in any kinde of sylver abouesaid whatsoeur in any of the said voyadge and that all such sylver as by vertue of this or graunte & lres Patente shall be shipped or laden by the said Gournor & Company or their successors to be transported out of this Realme in any of the said voyage, shall from tyme to tyme at the settinge forth of eury such pticuler voyadge be shipped or laden att the Porte or Havens of London Darmouth or Plymouth, or at some of the same porte or havens, & at no other porte or haven whatsoeur

This priuiledg shall not extend into any place being in the actuall possession of any prince in league or amytie wth her matie: wthin this or Realme or the dominions thereof and that all & eury such syluer as from tyme to tyme shall be shipped & laden in the said Porte of London Dartmouth or Plymouth, or any of them to be by force of theis presente transported out of this Realme as2 aforesaid shall from tyme to tyme be dulie entered by the Customer Comptroller Collector or other officer to whome yt shall appteyne of eury such Porte or Haven where the same shall happen to be shipped or laden in the Custome booke belonging to the said porte or Haven before such tyme as the same shall be shipped or laden to be transported as aforesaid wthout any Custome or subsydie to be paied for the same. And that in like manner all & all manner of gould & sylver whatsoeur wch shall be brought into this realme or any of or dominions by the said Gournor & Companie or any of them accordinge to the true meaneinge of theis presente shall be likewyse3 from tyme to tyme dulie entered by the Customer Comptroller or other officer of eury such Porte Creeke or place where the same gould or silver shall happen to be vnshipped or brought to land before such tyme as the same gould or silver, or any pte thereof shall be vnshipped or brought to land as ys aforesaid. PROUIDED alwaies neurtheles & or will & pleasure is that theis or lres Patente or any thinge therein Conteyned shall not in any sorte extend to giue or
graunte any lycence power or aucthoritie vnto the said Gournor & Company of mrchaunte of London trading into the East Indies or to any of them to vndertake or addresse any trade vnto any Countrie Port, Iland, Haven, Cittie, Creeke Towne or place being alreadie in the lawfull & actuall possession of any such Christian Prince or state as at this present is or at any tyme heereafter shall be in league or amytie wth vs or heires or successors, or wch doth not or will not accept of such trade but doth ouertlie declare and publishe the same to be vtterlie against his or their good will & likeing any thinge beinge1 before in theis presente conteyned to the Contrarie thereof notwthstandinge.

If this priviledge be found vnproffitable for the Realme then wthin 2 yeares warning geven vnder ye privie seale the same shall be voyde, but yf it shalbe found beneficiall then ye same to be renewed wth some addicons &c: Prouided alsoe that yf yt shall heereafter appeare to vs or heires or successors that this graunte, or the Continuance thereof in the wholle or in any pete thereof shall not be pffitable to vs or or heires and successors & to this or Realme that then and from from thenceforth vpon & after two yeares warneinge to be geven to the said Company by vs or heires or successors vnder or or their priuie seale or signe Manuell, this present graunt shall cease, be voied, and determined to all entente construccõns & purposes. And further of or espetiall grace certeine knowledg & meere mocõn we haue Condescended and graunted, and by theis presente for vs or heires and successors doe Condescend & graunte to the said Gournor & Company of mrchaunte of London trading into the East Indies & their successors that yf att the end of the said tearme of fifteene yeares yt shall seeme meete & Convenient vnto the said Gournor & Company or any the peties aforesaid that this present graunte shall be continued. And yf that alsoe it shall appeare vnto vs or heires and successors that the Continuance thereof shall not be preiudiciall or hurtfull to this or Realme but that we shall finde the further continuance thereof proffitable for vs or heires and successors and for our Realme wth such Condicõns as are herein mencioned, or wth some alteracõn or qualificacõn thereof that then we or heires or successors at the instaunce and humble peticõn of the said Gournor and Company or any of them
to be made vnto vs or heires & successors will graunte and make vnto the said Gournor and Company or any of them soe suing for the same and such other pson or psons or1 subiecte as they shall nominate and appointe or shall be by vs or heires or successors newly nominated not exceedinge in number fower & Twentie new łres Patente vnder the greate seale of England in due forme of lawe wth like graunte couenante2 clauses & articles as in theis presente are conteyned or wth addicõn of other necessarie articles or changeinge of theis into some other parte for and duringe the full terme of ffyfteene yeares then next followinge Willinge hereby and streightlie chardgeinge and Comaundeinge all & singuler or Admiralls viceadmiralls Iustices Maiors Sheriffe Escheators Cunstables bayliffe and all & singuler other or Officers ministers leidgmen and subiecte whatsoeur to be aydeinge favoringe helpeing and assistinge vnto the said Gournor and Company and to their successors and to their deputies officers ffactors servaunte assignes & mynisters and eury of them in executeing and enioyeinge the premisses aswell on land as on Sea from tyme to tyme when you or any of you shall there vnto be required any statute, acte, ordenance provisoe proclamačon or restrainte heretofore had made sett forth ordeyned or puided, or any other matter cause or thinge whatsoeur to the Contrarie in any wyse notwthstandinge Although expresse menčon of the true yearelie value or certeinetie of the premisses or of any of them, or of any other Guifte or graunte by vs or any of or progenitors to the said Gournor & Company of mrchaunte of London tradinge into the East Indies, or to any of them before this tyme made in theis presente is not made Or any statute Acte ordenaunce pvision pclamačon or restrainte to the Contrary hereof heretofore had, made, ordeyned or puided, or any other thinge cause or matter whatsoeur in any wyse notwthstandinge.
In Witnes whereof wee haue caused theis or łres to be made Patente Witnes or selfe att Westminster the xxxith day of December in the three & forteth yeare of or Reigne
p łre de privato sigillo &ca Huberd.

item.note: This is the famous first Charter of the Company, granted by Queen Elizabeth on the last day of the sixteenth century. In the absence of the original (of the fate of which nothing is known) the above is the oldest and most authoritative version in the India Office collection. There is another manuscript copy among the "Parchment Records" (No. 2), but it is of later date, and, so far as can be judged, of inferior
Afterwards Sir John Watts, Sheriff in 1596-97, and Mayor in 1606-7. He was governor of the Company from 11th April, 1601, to 6th July, 1602.

Whilom (1583) a pioneer of trade in the East, in company with Fitch and Newbery, though he did not himself go farther than Bassora; now "a graue, rich and principall Citizen" (Purchas). He was a large subscriber to the early voyages of the Company, and one of the first committees (see page 169).
Iuxon (Harl. MS. and Parch. Rec.); Jackson (Purchas).

Maurice Abbott, brother of George, Archbishop of Canterbury, and of Robert, Bishop of Salisbury. In 1615 he visited the East Indies; and on his return was made deputy governor of the Company, to which post he was re-elected 8 times. He was one of those appointed to treat with the Dutch Commissioners in London in 1619, and in the following year was sent, with Sir Dudley Digges, on a special
embassy to Holland on the same business. He became governor of the Company in March, 1624, and held that post until some time in 1638 or 1639, the period of his mayoralty. He was a member of parliament for several years, and spoke often in defence of the Company. He was knighted on the accession of Charles I., who, some 14 years later, made him "king's lieutenant" of London and suburbs during his Majesty's absence in the expedition against the Scots. He died 10th Jan., 1641/2.

For non-payment of his adventure (see Court Minutes of that date). Curiously enough the marginal entry occurs in all four texts; possibly it had been noted on the original charter.
Anto. Stratford should follow this name (Harl. MS., Parch. Rec. and Purchas).

Richard Wright was the first secretary of the Company, mention being made of him in that capacity on the 8th Oct., 1600, and he was still secretary in July, 1602. The loss of the second Court Book prevents us from saying how long he held this post, but there is reason to think that it could not have been to a later date than July, 1606. In 1615 he married the widow of John Stockley, who had been also a freeman of the Company, and a committee in 1608-10. Mrs. Stockley seems to have been a woman of some wealth, for at her husband's funeral the governor, deputy and committees were invited to dinner (Court Minutes, 29th Jan., 1614), and in the same year she adventured £1200 in the Company's stock (Ibid., 18th Feb., 1614). On 13th May, 1618, "Lyonell, son of Richard Wright, of Walthamstow," was admitted to the freedom of the Company, and as the admission was by patrimony, this entry probably relates to a son of the whilom secretary.

div.head: Agreement between the Company and William Cobreth for the Voyage to the North West, 20th April, 1602
An agreemt1 wth Willm Cobreth for discoury of the Norwest Passadge wth C:2 Waymouth.
div.p: His Indenture made the xxth day of Aprill Anno Dni 1602. & in the 44th yeare of the Reigne of or soureigne Ladie Elizabeth by the grace of god Queene of England ffraunce & Ireland defendor of the faith &c: Betweene Thomas Cambell of London Alderman on thone ptie & Willm Cobreth of Ratliffe in the Countie of Midds̄ Mariner on thother ptye. Witnesseth that whereas a crteine voyadge is prtended by godę grace, to be made from hence into the Norwest pte of China, Cataia, or Iapan or any other land in the latitude of 50 Degres Northward in the pte of 3 beyond the Seas. It is Couenanted, condescended, and now fullie agreed by and betweene the said pties to theis presente in manner and forme following that is to saie. The said Willm Cobreth for him his Executors and Administrators & for euery of them doth Couenant and graunte to and wth the said Thomas Cambell his Executors & Administrators & eury of them by theis prsente. That he the said Willm Cobreth shall and will be readie in the Cittie of London & goe on the said voyadge, & therein Contynue for the discoury of the said Norwest pte, from hence of China Cataia or Iapan or any other land in the latitude of 50 Degres Northward at the Comaundemt will & appointmt of Capt: George Waymouth in such a ship as the same Capten shall thinke good. And on the same voyadge shall proceede and saile effectuallie to thutmost of his skill or knowledg wthout fraude or Coven, and not depte or goe from the said voyadge wthout the spetiall lycence of the said Capt: George Waymouth first had and obtayned in that behalfe. In Consideracõn whereof the said Willm Cobreth hath receiued in hand at thensealeing & deliury hereof the some of xxli of &c: in pte of paymt of his wages for the said pretended voyadge, whereof he acknowleth himselfe fullie satisfied and contented. And the said Thomas Cambell for him his [executors] and Adminī & for eury of them doth Couenante & graunte to & wth the said Willm Cobreth his Executors & Admin̄ by theis prsente That he the said

div.p: Thomas Cambell his Execū or Asss shall well and trulie paie or cause to be paid vnto the said Wilłm Cobreth his Execū or Asss vpon the discoury of the said Norwest passadg or pte of China, Cataia, or Iapan, or any other land in the latitude of 50 Degres Northward and retourne from thence into the Realme of England the some of six pounde of &c, for eury monneth that the said Wilłm Cobreth shall be vpon the said voyadge (the said xxli paid in hand as aforesaid being reconed as pte & pcell thereof [ ]). Provided alwaies that yf the said Wilłm Cobreth & his Comp. shall not fortune to discour the said Norwest pte of China, Cataia or Iapan or any other Land in the Latitude of 50 Degres Northward as aforesaid : Then the said Thomas Cambell his Execū or Assignes shall well & trulie paie or cause to be paid vnto the said Wilłm Cobreth his Executors or Assignes, onelie the some of iijli of &c: for eury monneth that the said Wilłm Cobreth shall be vpon the said voyadge the said xxli paid in hand as aforesaid being alwaies accompted as pte & pcell thereof. In Witnes &c:

div.head: A Coppie of a łre of Reprisall for the East Indian Marchaunte.1
div.p:
Charles Earle of Notingham2 Baron of Effingham knight of the most noble order of the Garter, Lord Leiuetenante of her maties Counties of Sussex & Surrey Constable of hir mate honor3 and Castle of Windsor Ld : High Admirall of England Ireland and Wales and the Dominions & Iles of the same, Of the Towne of Callis & mrches thereof Normandy Gascoyne and Guines & Capteine Genrall of her maties Seas & Navy royall. To all Christian People to whome theis presente shall come or other wyse appteyne greeting in or Lord god eurlasting. Whereas or souereigne Lady
Elizabeth by the grace of god Queene of England ffraunce & Ireland defendor of the faith &c : beinge Crediblie adverticed that the kinge of Spaine hath of late made staye of the shipps goode & mrchandizes of hir maties : loueing subiecte wthin the Realme of Spaine & Portingale & other places of his Dominions, & hath caused them their1 being for the trade of mrchandizes to be reteyned & kept in prizon Contrary to the order of Lawe & Iustice. Upon the humble and pitifull sute of hir maties said subiecte the mrchaunte owners & others interessed in the said ships goode and psonns soe stayed made to hir matie for łres of Reprisalls to be graunted vnto them and that they not haueing any other meanes by order of Iustice to be yealded vnto them might by lycenced to stay apprehend and take the shipps goode & mrchandizes of the kinge of Spaine, or any his Subiecte wheresoeur vpon the Seas to aunsweare and satisfie the losse and damadge by them susteyned by reason of their ships and goode soe taken and reteyned hath by her maties : łres Patente beareing date the ninth day of Iulie— 1585. vnder her maties : seale willed and authorized me as hir mate Admirall to graunt Comission for the apprehending and takeing the shipps goode & mrchandizes of the kinge of Spaine, or any his subiecte to such hir mates loueing subiecte soe dampnified & in such manner and forme and according to such articles & orders as by the lorde & others of her mate privie Councell or by any six of them should be agreed vpon & set downe vnder their hande. And whereas tenn of the Lorde & others of her maties : privy Councell haue agreed upon Certeine articles & orders in that behalfe & haue set downe the same in writeing vnder their hande & haue deliuered the same to me for my direcc̃on herein wch arcles & orders be & remaine wth me of recorde. And whereas further the Gournor and Assistante & Companie of the mrchaunte of London trading for the East Indies, haue made proofe before me that certeine of their goode shipps & mrchandizes, were of late stayed arrested & deteyned in the pte of Spaine by the kinge order & authoritie there, & that the losse & damadge thereof vnto them by reason of the said stay & seasure ariseing doth amounte to the some of 2000li ster: or thearaboute wherevpon the said Gournor & Assistaunte & Company of the mrchaunte of London trading for
the East Indies aforesaid haue reedy victualled & furnished to the Seas one Shipp Called the Suzan1 of London of the burthen of 250 Tonnes or thereaboutes whereof Iohn Havard goeth Capteine & Samuell Spencer mr wth mariners & menn of Warr being victualled for monnethes & furnished wth Caste peeces & haue likewyse entred into bond in hir maties high Courte of the Admiralty that neither the said shipp nor any the Company thereof shall not attempt against any hir maties loueing subiecte the subiecte of the ffrentch kinge the kinge of Scotland Denmarke or Sweden or any the Inhabitants of the United provinces of the Haunce Townes or lowe Countries or the subiecte of any other Prince or potentate being in good league and amity wth her matie, but onelie against the Subiecte of the kinge of Spaine: And alsoe shall bring or cause to be brought all such shipps goode or mrchandizes as they shall soe take & apprehend of the kinge of Spaine or any his subiecte together wth three or fower of the Company of eury such prize as shall be of most accompte whereof the mr & Pilott to be twoe to some porte of this hir maties Realme of England as shall be most Convenient for them, And shall not breake, bulke, waste, spoyle, sell or diminish any such shipps & goode soe taken vntill the shall be adiudged in hir maties high Courte of the Admiraltie to be lawfull prize. And therevpon an Inventorie to be taken by the viceadmirall of the place or his Deputie & other publique Officers of the same, And appraisment made of the same goode by some six honest menn Inhabitante of the said Porte where they shall soe arriue, and that the same Inventory & appraismt shall be retourned into hir maties high Courte of the Admiraltie wthin six weeke then next ensueing. Know ye therefore that I the said Charles Earle of Notingham Lord High Adll aforesaid by vertue of her maties said łres Pattente to me directed doe lycence and authorize the said Gournor & Assistaunte & Company of the mrchaunte of London trading for the East Indies to sett forth to the Seas the said shipp called the Suzan, soe as is aforesaid
furnished & munited and therewth to sett vpon and by force of Armes to staie & apprehend of the ships goode & mrchandizes of the kinge of Spaine, or any his subiecte in as ample manner as if it were in the tyme of open warr betwixt her matie: & the said kinge of Spaine, & the said ships goode & mrchandizes soe taken and brought into some porte of this hir maties Realme of England, & thereof an Inventory taken, appraismt made & iudgmt geven in the said high Courte of the Admtie: in the said high Courte of the Admiralty for the Approbac̃on of the same to be agood & lawfull prize in manner & forme aforesaid. Then the said ships goode & mrchandizes to keepe and reteyne in his or their possession & to make sale & dispose thereof in open mrkett or howsoeur els to their best benefitt in as ample & beneficiall manner, as if the said ships goode & mrchandizes had bene Come by, through the lawfull traffique & trade of mrchaunte or of iust prize in the tyme of open warr betwixt hir matie & the said kinge of Spaine soe that neither the said Capteine master nor any the Company thereof that shall in his or their owne psonn serue in the shipp aforesaid, or otherwyse bear Chardge in the Adventure, or in any other sorte further or sett forewarde the said enterprize in manner & forme aforesaid, shall not be reputed or challendged for any offendor against hir maties lawes and that alsoe it shall be lawfull for any manner of pson to buye the said ships goode & mrchandizes soe as aforesaid taken prayzed Inventoryed & adiudged wthout any daunger losse hindraunce trouble molestac̃on or incumbraunce whatsoeur Provided alwaies that yf by Color of this Comission there shall be taken any shipps goode or mrchandizes of any hir maties: loueing subiecte the subiecte of the ffrench kinge, the kinge of Scotland Denmarke or Sweden or any the Inhabitante of the united prouinces of the hance Townes or lowe Countries or the subiecte of any other Prince or Potentate being in good league & amity wth hir matie & the same or any other shipps taken by authoritie hereof shalbe spoyled sould imbeaselled or dyminished before they shall be adiudged in her maties high Courte of the Adty: to belong to the king of Spaine, or any of his subiecte that then this Comission to be void and of noe sufficient authoritie, either to take the said shipps & goode or to warrante
or saue harmlesse such as shall receiue, bye or intermeddle therein, but that alsoe both the prizes soe taken, & the shipps of warr shall be Confiscate to or vse. Prouided alsoe that the said shipps goode and mrchandizes soe as is aforesaid, after an Inventory taken, appraismt made & iudgment geven in manner and forme aforesaid shall be equallie devided into three pte, whereof one pte to goe to the mrchaunte & owners of the said shipp, another pte to the victuallers & the third parte to the Captaine master mariners & souldiers thereof. Provided further that this Comission shall remaine and be in force during this their present voyadg, & noe longer In witnes whereof I haue herevnto caused the greate seale of myne office to be affixed: Yeven at London in hir maties high Courte of the Adty aforesaid the 23th day of Aprill. 1601. And in the 43th yeare of the Reigne of or soureigne Lady Elizabeth by the grace of god Queene of England ffraunce & Ireland defendor of the faith &c :

This commission is only for the one vessel, the Susan. But in the letter of instructions to the Judge of the Admiralty Court, which follows the present document, all the four ships are mentioned. It seems probable therefore that a separate commission was issued for each ship, of which this particular one was entered as a specimen.

div.head: Letter from the Lord High Admiral to the Judge of the Admiralty Court, ordering the preparation of the preceding Commission, 14th
A łre from the Earle of Nottingham to mr Ceasar1 Iudge of the high Courte of the Adty :
div.p: Mr Ceasar the marchaunte of London haueing prepared fower good shipps for the voyadg to the East Indies in the trade of mrchandizes haue beene sutors vnto me2 for Comission to take any shipps or goode belonging to the king of Spaine or to any of his subiecte either in their way outwarde, or in their retourne, wch I haue beene Contented to graunte vnto them. Therefore I doe pray you to cause Comission to be drawen for them, to furnish vnto the

item.note: See note 2, page 25.

Nothing can be traced in the Court Minutes as to this application. The only reference to the matter is under date of 22nd Jan., 1600/1, when, the question having been raised of the mariners' share "upon such reprisals as may happen in the "voyage," it was answered that there was "no intention to make any attempt for "reprisals, but only to pursue the voyage in a merchantlike course. Yet notwith- "standing if any opportunity be offered without prejudice or hazard of the said "voyage" Captain Lancaster was to take such course therein as he should think meet.

div.head: Lres Pattente1 for transportacõn of 20000li in money to the Gournor of East India 1606.
div.p:
JAMES by the grace of God kinge of England ffraunce and Ireland defendor of the faith &c: To all to whome theis presente shall come greetinge. Wheareas or late deare sister Q: Elizabeth by her łres Patente vnder the greate seale of England beareing date at Westminster the xxxjth day of Decemb in the xliijth yeare of her Reigne vpon peticõn made vnto her by diurs her loueing Subiectę, for her Royall assent and lycence to be graunted vnto them. That they at their owne Adventure Costę and Chardgę aswell for the Honor of this Realme of England, as for increase of Navigacõn & Advancemt of Trade of mrchandize wthin the same, might Adventure and set forth crteine voyadgę wth a Convenient nomber of shipps and Pinnaces by way of Traffique & mrchandize into the East Indies in the Countries and Portę of Asia & Africa did incorporate the said Peticioners into abodie pollitique by the name of the Gournor and Companie of the mrchauntę of London trading to the East Indies. To haue hould and enioye the sole benefitt of the trade and traffique of the said East Indies for the space of xv yeares from the byrth of or Lord God then last past before the date of the said łres Patente. And
whereas by the same lres Patente lycence was graunted to the said Gournor and Companie of mrchaunte of London tradinge into the East Indies to transporte out of this Realme into the said Indies in eury of their voyadge duringe the said terme of 15 yeares all such fforreigne Coyne of silver, spanish or other fforraine sylver, or bullion of sylver, as they should duringe the said tearme bringe or cause to be brought into this Realme of England, from the pte beyond the Seas, either in the same kinde, stampe, sorte or fashion, wch yt should haue when they brought it in, or in any other forme, stampe, or fashion coyned in the Mynte wthin the Tower of London; soe as the whole quantities of Coyne or moneys by them to be transported in any their said voyage during the said tearme should not exceed the value of 30000li in any one voyadge, and soe as the some of vjm poundes at the least pcell of the said some or value of 30000li to be transported as aforesaid should be first Coyned wthin the same Tower of London, before the same might be transported in any of the said voyadge as by the said lres Patente more at lardge appeareth.

Now forasmuch as the said Gournor and Companie of the said mrchante since the said lres Patente to them graunted, haue made 2 seurall voyadge into the said East Indies, & retourned their ships from thence laden wth sundrie kinde of mrchandizes pffitable for or kingdomes, and haue alsoe prepared & are readie to set forth an other voyadge into the said East Indies, & haue humblie besought by petiñon, & shewed vnto vs, that by experience they haue formrlie found that they could not wthout greate difficultie, & losse vnto them in the value of their moneys new coyned, make trade for their mrchandize into the said East Indies, because they were not such as the people of those pte were acquainted wthall: but stamped wth an Image or supscripc̃on straunge & vnknowne vnto them.1 And that they haue beene and are desierous by all good meanes to manadge, & carrie their said trade as neare as they Cann for the benefitt of or kingdomes and dominions rather by the transportac̃on of the Natiue Comodities of the same and by bartringe & exchaunge of them for fforreine Comodities wch now they purpose more
lardglie to attempt and haue good hope to accomplish, then by vsing the whole libertie graunted to them by the said łres Patente for carrieing out of the full some of 30000li in eury voyadge in manner aforesaid. And that they will content them selues in this their now third entended voyadge into the East Indies, wth the liƀtie of transportinge xxmli onelie in forreine Coynes wthout transportac̃on of any other Coyne, bullion, or silver. In reguard whereof they did humblie pray in their said petic̃on that we would be graciouslie pleased to graunte them lycence that they may transporte the value of xxmli of forreine Coyne in this their entended voyadge, wthout new coyninge the same or any p̃te thereof. Know yee therefore that we favoringethe said mrchante, & being desierous to giue them all furtherance & encouradgmt to proceede & goe forward in their trade of or especiall grace, certeine knowledge and meere moc̃on, haue geven and graunted, and by theis presente for vs, or heires & Successors doe giue and graunte lycence vnto the said Gournor and Companie of mrchaunte of London tradinge into the East Indies. That it shall and may be lawfull for them their factors & Assignes in his1 now prtended voyadge into the East Indies to transporte out of this or Realme of England all such forreine Coine or sylver, either spannish or other forreine silver, as they haue prepared, p̃cured, or gotten, or shall prepare p̃cure or gett being alredie brought or to be brought from the parte beyond the seas, before the depture of their shipps out of the Ryver of Thames. Soe as the whole quantitie of the Coyne and moneys by them to be transported in this their prsent intended voyadge towarde the said East Indies, doe not exceed the said value of 20000li. The same to be transported in the same kinde, sorte, stampe, or fashion, as the said moneys, are or shall be p̃cured, gotten, or brought into this Realme of England, and that wthout any new coyninge or altringe the said moneys or any p̃te thereof, from the stampe it beareth, any statute restrainte or p̃hibic̃on in that behalfe made to the Contrarie in any wyse notwthstandinge. In Witnes whereof we haue caused theis or łres to be made Patente. Witnes or selfe at Westminster the vth day of Ianuarie
in the 4th yeare of or Reigne of England ffraunce & Ireland, & of Scotland the xlth.1
Ravencroft p̄ b̄re de priuato sigillo &c:

div.head: Letters Patent exempting spices and drugs sold by the Company for re-exportation from the operation of the statute for the well ga
A Coppie2 of the Patent for mitigacõn of the Statute for garbling spices.
div.p:
JAMES by the grace of God king of England Scotland ffraunce and Ireland defendor of the faith &c: To or high Treasurer, and Admirall of England, and to all other or Admiralls Viceadmiralls Captaines and others seruinge vpon the Sea. And to all Maiors Sheriffe Constables Customers Comptrollers Surveyor Searchers, Keeps of or Porte, Creeke and Passadge and to all others or Officers Ministers, and subiecte whatsoeur to whome in that behalfe it shall or may appteyne and to eury of them greetinge. Wheareas in the first Session of or Parliament holden at Westminster, in the first yeare of or Reigne of England ffraunce and Ireland and of Scotland the seaven and thirteth one Acte3 was made intituled an Acte for the well garbling of Spices wheareby it was ordeyned & enacted that from and after the last day of September then next ensueing the end of that Session of Parliamte, All spices wares drugge and other mrchandizes garbleable, that is to say Pepp, Cloues, Mace, Nutmegge, Cynamon, Ginger Long Pepper, Wormeseede4, Comynseede, Annyseede, Colyanderseede, Bynny pepp Almonde
Date Galles Gumes of all sorte and kinde garbleable Spikenard Galingath1 Turmericke, Setweth2 Cassia fistula Gynny Pepp
